name: Nethe
myth: Nethe was a shag who sat on the rock below the cliffs and would not go in when the rain came. She held her wings out to dry, and they were never dry, and she said so, and the other birds laughed at her. Tavo the Gale heard the laughing and came down to see. He blew on her wings until they were nearly dry, then sent a squall to wet them again, because that is his way. Ennu the Kite-Wright, mending a sail on the shingle, said nothing. She handed Nethe a corner of cloth and showed her how to hold it against the wind so the wet would run off. Mother Hesk marked her down among those who wait. Now when your coat is heavy and your hands are cold, look up. Nethe is there with her wings out. Wait a little. The rock will be dry in the morning.
verse:
Wet wings on the rock
she holds them out to the wind
they dry by morning
